paper_title: Mechanistic Understanding and Mitigation of Language Confusion in   English-Centric Large Language Models
caption: Distribution of Important Neurons Associated with Confusion Points in Llama3-8B. (a) Distribution of the top 300 most important FFN neurons across layers for an individual Chinese prompt “UTF8gbsn请解释拆东墙补西墙的意思。(Please explain `UTF8gbsn拆东墙补西墙.')” from Aya. (b) Aggregated distribution of important neuron scores across all Chinese test samples in Aya.
model_annotation: The two line graphs illustrate the distribution of important feed-forward network (FFN) value neurons associated with confusion points in the Llama3-8B model, with the x-axis representing the layer number ranging from 0 to 35 in increments of 5, and the y-axis representing the count of neurons, scaled linearly from 0 to 100 in graph (a) and from 0 to 175 in graph (b). In graph (a), titled "Individual Case," the blue line with circular markers shows that the count of Llama3 FFN value neurons remains at 0 from layer 0 to layer 14, then begins to increase gradually, reaching a value of approximately 80 at layer 30. In graph (b), titled "Aggregated Neuron Scores," the green line with circular markers remains at a low count, fluctuating slightly around 0 to 10 from layer 0 to layer 28, then rises sharply to a count of approximately 170 at layer 32.

model_annotations.English: The figure presents two line plots illustrating the distribution of important feed-forward network (FFN) neurons associated with confusion points in the Llama3-8B model, as analyzed in the context of English-centric language models. In plot (a), labeled "Individual Case," the x-axis represents the model's layer number, ranging from 0 to 30 with increments of 5, while the y-axis, labeled "count," measures the number of neurons, ranging from 0 to 100. The plot shows a single line, colored blue with circular markers, representing the "Llama3 FFN value neurons." This line remains near zero for layers 0 through 25, with a sharp increase starting at layer 26, where the count jumps to approximately 20, and continues to rise steeply, reaching a peak of 80 at layer 30. In plot (b), labeled "Aggregated Neuron Scores," the x-axis again represents the layer number, but extends from 0 to 35 with increments of 5. The y-axis, also labeled "count," ranges from 0 to 175. This plot features a single green line with circular markers, corresponding to the "Llama3 FFN value neurons." The count remains relatively stable and low, fluctuating between 0 and 10, for layers 0 through 28. At layer 29, the count increases to approximately 50, and then rises sharply to a peak of about 175 at layer 32 before the data ends.
